claims.text: Setting the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service enables Terraform and OpenTofu to use self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
`PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is the environment variable that specifies the domain serving the Terraform-compatible API in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud (e.g. `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`).
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered.
For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the DNS record for the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` domain should point at the same host that serves `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN`.
A separate domain for `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is not required: it can be set to the same value as `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.

The Pulumi state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the Terraform-compatible API domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, `terraform login`/`tofu login` commands, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
The page /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ exists as a state backend guide for Terraform and OpenTofu.
In self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name, `terraform login`, and `tofu login` are used with the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` value as the hostname.
